title: Routes registry
description: data/registry/routes.json: makers' APIs, resellers, hosts, routers, harnesses, self-hosting, with their dated level maps and defaults (DATA-PIPELINE §4).

operator.description: The maker running it (maker-api, reseller of its own models), or null.

spellings.description: How sources name this route (a provider name, a flag), so a route fact without a term resolves; matched exactly, case-insensitively.

name_prefixes.description: Prefixes written before ids of this namespace (Inspect / LiteLLM provider prefixes: 'anthropic/', 'openai/' for maker-api; 'openrouter/' for openrouter). Stripped once when resolving a name in this namespace; the head of a `prefix` value is looked up here, which also names the route.

names_case_insensitive.description: Names registered in this route's namespace match case-insensitively (casefold), after the prefix is stripped: the Hugging Face namespace (`huggingface`), where repository ids are case-insensitive ('qwen/qwen3.8-27b' is 'Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B'). Absent / false: exact match.

items.description: How the route maps a level, dated.

ties.description: Tie handling for nearest-supported (ambiguous per DATA-PIPELINE §4).

via.description: For a harness: the next step this record applies to (the route the harness hands the call to: maker-api, openrouter, bedrock…). Absent: every next step. A harness maps a level per provider (its provider adapter), so its records name the provider (registry fix, 26 Oct 2026).

maker.description: For a harness: the maker whose models this record applies to (a provider adapter of the harness: Inspect's anthropic provider on the maker's API). Absent: every maker.

models.description: The model keys this record applies to (absent: every model of `maker`, or every model).
Model key → what the route does with it.

additionalProperties.description: What a route does with one model.

ids.description: The route's ids for the model.

name.description: The route's id for the model.

via.description: For a harness: the next step this record applies to (the route the harness hands the call to: maker-api, openrouter, bedrock…). Absent: every next step. A harness maps a level per provider (its provider adapter), so its records name the provider (registry fix, 26 Oct 2026).

mapping.description: Documented mapping requested → served (identity entries when documented as identity).

via.description: For a harness: the next step this record applies to (the route the harness hands the call to: maker-api, openrouter, bedrock…). Absent: every next step. A harness maps a level per provider (its provider adapter), so its records name the provider (registry fix, 26 Oct 2026).

default.description: The route's own documented default for the model (routers and hosts; DATA-PIPELINE §5.1 step 7).

items.description: A route default for the model, dated (optionally per next step).

via.description: For a harness: the next step this record applies to (the route the harness hands the call to: maker-api, openrouter, bedrock…). Absent: every next step. A harness maps a level per provider (its provider adapter), so its records name the provider (registry fix, 26 Oct 2026).

mapping.description: Route-wide documented mapping requested → served, dated (a harness's provider adapter: Inspect sends max as xhigh to OpenRouter). Read after the model's own `mapping` and before its `accepts`; filtered by `via`, `maker` and `models`.

via.description: For a harness: the next step this record applies to (the route the harness hands the call to: maker-api, openrouter, bedrock…). Absent: every next step. A harness maps a level per provider (its provider adapter), so its records name the provider (registry fix, 26 Oct 2026).

maker.description: For a harness: the maker whose models this record applies to (a provider adapter of the harness: Inspect's anthropic provider on the maker's API). Absent: every maker.

models.description: The model keys this record applies to (absent: every model of `maker`, or every model).

label_as_level.description: A closed harness that shows a level label without documenting what it sends: the maintainer's standing rule `closed-harness-label` (26 Oct 2026) takes the label as the level sent, flagged `harness-label-as-level:<route>`, as LMArena's labels. Applies only where the harness documents nothing for the run (a dated mapping, accepts or level mapping wins); the call then reaches the maker's API.
